input.content:
# word_count fix

## Root cause

`word_count` used `text.split(" ")`. Splitting on an explicit single-space separator keeps empty strings: `"".split(" ")` is `['']` (count 1), and `"a  b".split(" ")` is `['a', '', 'b']` (count 3). It also treated tabs and newlines as part of a word and counted leading/trailing spaces as extra words.

## Fix

Changed `textutils.py` to use `text.split()` with no argument. Python then splits on any run of whitespace and drops leading/trailing whitespace, so no empty strings are produced. An empty or whitespace-only string returns `[]`, so the count is 0.

## Test

Added `tests/test_word_count.py`, covering:
- `""` → 0 and `"a  b"` → 2 (the reported cases)
- whitespace-only `"   "` → 0
- leading/trailing spaces `"  a b  "` → 2
- tabs and newlines `"a\tb\nc"` → 3

All five failed before the fix. After it, the full suite passes (`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`).
